LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: NOTE MAKING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we make notes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify key points in a text for information
2. appreciate the role of making summaries in reading

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: NOTE MAKING
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: NOTE MAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify key points in a text for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify key points in a text for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify key points in a text for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify key points in a text for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of making summaries in reading

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of making summaries in reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of making summaries in reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of making summaries in reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify key points in a text for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of making summaries in reading)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify key points in a text for information.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of making summaries in reading.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we make notes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Information: Note Making means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify key points in a text for information.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of making summaries in reading.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
